headline: Chuba Bucky Doo Escapes King Henry Again by 1.2 — For the Second Straight Week, a Bench Call Decides It
meme_brief: A guy loses back-to-back games by roughly a single point, both times because he left a 40-plus point player on his bench — this week it was a 45-point quarterback sitting the pine while his team lost by 1.2.
recap:
Chuba Bucky Doo beat Long Live King Henry 128.4 to 127.2, the second straight week the two Hearts division rivals have decided their game by almost exactly one point. Jaxon Smith-Njigba single-handedly kept Chuba Bucky Doo alive with 43 points, while King Henry's Jared Goff sat on the bench and put up 45.05 — the single most damaging bench decision in the league this week, a 18.25-point gap between Goff and the Jalen Hurts start that replaced him. King Henry has now benched two different 40-plus scorers in as many weeks and has nothing to show for it.

The rest of the board wasn't as close. Broke Dak Mountain ran up 122.5 behind a 54.3-point outing from Josh Allen — the league's top individual scorer for a second straight week — and blew out Pukachu Chews You 122.5 to 74.45, the week's biggest margin at 48.05 points. Pukachu Chews You is 0-2 and dead last in points scored. Dak to the Future stayed unbeaten, riding a 44.55-point Dak Prescott performance to a 138.45-106.7 win over Meredith's Fan Club, who got 41.8 from Patrick Mahomes and still lost by nearly 32 — the same story as last week, a big quarterback number wasted on a losing roster.

demon44 also moved to 2-0, beating Silverbacks 115.55-98.6 behind Jonathan Taylor's 29.2. Silverbacks compounded the loss by sitting Bryce Young, who scored 35.95 points from the bench, in favor of a 14.8-point day from Justin Herbert — a 21.15-point gap, and the second week running that a Silverbacks-adjacent bench call has been a headline. Screaming Eagles fell to 0-2 in almost identical fashion to their Week 1 loss, sitting Matthew Stafford's 43.25 in favor of an 11.1-point Drake Maye start, a 32.15-point gap that was the single worst bench decision in the league this week.

The league's top scorer overall was Josh Allen at 54.3, part of Broke Dak Mountain's rout. Waffle House also won comfortably, 118.95-97.9 over mikelanta, despite mikelanta actually outscoring several winning teams over the season — a pattern now worth watching heading into the playoff math below.
transaction_desk:
It was a quiet week on the wire — no waiver priority actually changed hands, since every move logged was an uncontested pickup. mikelanta added Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, dropping Keaton Mitchell, and got 11.45 points out of him in his first week aboard — cheap production at zero cost, which fits the pattern: mikelanta's Week 1 add of Ted Hurst has quietly produced 8.8 points and the Las Vegas Raiders defense has produced 16, both for free.

Pukachu Chews You added Dylan Sampson, which shares a backfield and position with Quinshon Judkins already on that roster — a sensible injury-insurance pickup rather than a speculative flier, though it hasn't scored yet. demon44 continued its season-long habit of building entirely off the waiver wire, adding tight end Kenyon Sadiq, wide receiver Demarcus Robinson, and the Green Bay Packers defense, none of it costing any priority — the Packers add has already returned 9 points in its first week. Long Live King Henry picked up the Cincinnati Bengals defense for nothing and got a serviceable 12 points out of it, which is nice, but doesn't offset benching a 45-point quarterback the same week.

standings_narrative:
The three division leaders — Dak to the Future, demon44, and mikelanta — currently hold the top three playoff seeds by record, even though mikelanta is sitting at 1-1 while carrying the second-most points in the league. Chuba Bucky Doo and Long Live King Henry fill the next two seeds on record alone, both at 1-1. The final spot goes to Joe Mama Angie Daddy, who holds the points-based sixth seed at 259.15 for the season, edging out Waffle House's 246.75 on the bubble.

Everyone else — Silverbacks, Broke Dak Mountain, Screaming Eagles, Meredith's Fan Club, and Pukachu Chews You — sits outside the picture for now. Broke Dak Mountain's case is the most interesting: a 1-1 record with the league's best individual scorer in back-to-back weeks and a point differential nobody else in that group can touch, meaning one more result could reshuffle this quickly.
look_ahead: Week 3 pairs Chuba Bucky Doo against Waffle House, Joe Mama Angie Daddy against Meredith's Fan Club, and Broke Dak Mountain against Silverbacks. Long Live King Henry gets a break from its rivalry with Chuba Bucky Doo and instead faces mikelanta, whose scoring pace makes it a live threat regardless of record. Dak to the Future, still unbeaten, draws Screaming Eagles, who will need to actually start their high scorers this time. demon44 faces Pukachu Chews You, a get-well matchup for a winless team against a division leader that hasn't needed to spend anything to stay unbeaten.

running_jokes: The Chuba Bucky Doo / Long Live King Henry rivalry has now been decided by roughly a point in both meetings, both times traceable to a King Henry bench decision — Vele's numbers weren't the issue in Week 1, and Goff sitting for 45.05 wasn't the issue this week either, except that it obviously was.
Long Live King Henry has benched two separate 40-plus-point performances in two straight weeks and is 1-1 to show for it.
Screaming Eagles have benched a 40-plus-point quarterback in back-to-back weeks (Stafford twice now) and are 0-2.
demon44 remains undefeated on a roster built almost entirely from zero-cost waiver claims.
Broke Dak Mountain has produced the league's top individual scorer in consecutive weeks (Josh Allen twice) and has now converted one into a blowout win.
mikelanta's record continues to undersell it — second in the league in total points at 1-1.
Dak to the Future has led the league in points scored in both weeks played.
